claims_about_writeup.why: A manual word count of contribution.md yields roughly 230-240 words depending on how hyphenated terms and headers are counted, consistent with the stated 238.

message_source_quote: The reading list contains the White-Bear Steering paper (which solves almost exactly this setup), so I deliberately went beyond its construction
writeup_source_quote: recovers a direction at cosine 0.93-0.94 to the published white-bear direction

differences.message_quote: The reading list contains the White-Bear Steering paper (which solves almost exactly this setup), so I deliberately went beyond its construction
differences.writeup_quote: recovers a direction at cosine 0.93-0.94 to the published white-bear direction
differences.what: The message explicitly names the source as 'White-Bear Steering paper' from the reading list and states it 'solves almost exactly this setup,' framing the relationship as building on/going beyond a near-identical prior solution; the write-up never names the paper or reading list, only citing 'the published white-bear direction' as a comparison data point within a 'What is new' robustness argument, without characterizing the prior work as solving nearly the same problem.

differences.message_quote: It used only the *think vs don't-think* pairs. I instead build the direction from the *concealment* conditions (secret / preference) against the hold-in-mind condition — never touching the don't-think pairs.
differences.writeup_quote: not an artifact of the think/don't-think wording
differences.what: The message explicitly describes the prior work's construction (think vs don't-think pairs only) and contrasts it point-by-point with the new concealment-based construction; the write-up only obliquely alludes to think/don't-think wording as one of several contrasts tested, without attributing that specific construction to the prior paper.

differences.message_quote: I tested several genuinely different constructions (self-authored implicature-vs-flat content contrast, a "name-vs-continue" contrast, an "infer-vs-plain" matched-carrier stance) — all failed, confirming how narrow the working axis is and motivating the pooled-concealment choice.
differences.what: The message cites additional failed alternative constructions as evidence of the narrowness/novelty of the working axis; the write-up contains no mention of these additional attempted constructions.

rationale: The write-up treats the prior white-bear direction only as a quantitative comparison point (cosine 0.93-0.94) within its own 'What is new' robustness argument, never naming the paper or stating that it addresses the same problem; the message explicitly names the 'White-Bear Steering paper,' says it 'solves almost exactly this setup,' and frames the contribution as deliberately going beyond its specific (think/don't-think) construction, plus adds extra failed-experiment evidence for novelty not present in the write-up.
